technical_principles.summary: Wrestling S&C should support stance, hand fighting, shots, sprawls, mat returns, rides, escapes, scrambles, and repeated high-intensity exchanges without destroying technical quality.
Neck, trunk, grip, upper-back, hip, adductor, posterior-chain, knee, and ankle capacity are central because wrestling creates high isometric and awkward-position demands.
The backend must not prescribe aggressive dehydration, starvation, or unsafe weight-cutting. Weight and body composition goals should bias toward safe nutrition and performance.

avoid_until_ready: stacking hard live wrestling and heavy lower-body work
high shot volume with knee/back irritation

drills_or_practice_design: towel row or rope climb progression
common_errors: using random fatigue circuits instead of wrestling-specific repeat effort
doing hard neck work before live wrestling
adding high-volume shots with knee or back pain
heavy lower-body lifting too close to competition
ignoring skin, hydration, sleep, and recovery issues
safety_constraints: Do not prescribe dehydration, starvation, or unsafe weight-cut practices.
Regress with neck, neurological, severe head, or radiating symptoms.
Reduce live volume and shot volume with knee, hip, groin, or low-back pain.
Avoid fatiguing neck/trunk before hard live wrestling.
Competition week should reduce soreness and preserve sharpness.

sport_training_rules.rule: Wrestling S&C should support stance, shots, sprawls, hand fighting, mat returns, rides, escapes, scrambles, and recovery between high-intensity exchanges.
recommended_action: Train relative strength, repeat power, grip, trunk, neck, hips, adductors, and aerobic support.
blocked_action: Do not replace wrestling conditioning with random fatigue circuits.

sport_training_rules.rule: Do not prescribe aggressive dehydration, starvation, or unsafe weight-cut practices. Bias toward performance, hydration, and safe nutrition guidance.
recommended_action: Use safe nutrition goals and refer severe weight-cut concerns to qualified professionals.
Avoid hard conditioning under dehydration or poor readiness.

planning_rules.rule: Competition week should reduce soreness, live volume, heavy eccentric work, and novelty while preserving stance, motion, first attacks, hand fighting, and sharpness.
recommended_action: Use short technical goes, mobility, light power primers, and recovery.
Keep favorite attacks and mat positions sharp without creating fatigue.

planning_rules.rule: Reduce live wrestling, high-volume shots, throws, and hard mat returns when pain or readiness signals are poor.
recommended_action: Use technical drilling, mobility, lower-impact conditioning, or strength work that avoids the painful pattern.
blocked_action: hard live goes with worsening neck, back, knee, shoulder, rib, or neurological symptoms

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build a physical base for wrestling without making stance, shots, sprawls, or mat skills sloppy.
progression_signals: no worsening joint or neck symptoms
keeps stance and motion under light fatigue

skill_assessments.summary: Assess wrestling readiness through completion, RPE, sleep/stress, pain response, shot/sprawl quality, live volume tolerance, and recovery.
hold_if: worsening knee, hip, groin, shoulder, rib, or back pain

minimum_evidence: any pain, readiness, or safety concern
hold_when: worsening knee, hip, groin, shoulder, rib, or back pain
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Reduce live wrestling and high-impact/high-fatigue work; bias toward technical drilling, mobility, safe strength, or recovery.
